title: A uniform alternating class
statement: Let $b\in\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}$ and $i\in\mathbb N$. Let $V$ be a language in polynomial time, let $f$ be a polynomial-time computable function on bit strings, and let $\ell$ map bit strings to natural numbers with $y\mapsto 1^{\ell(y)}$ polynomial-time computable. Then the language of strings $y$ for which the depth-$i$ alternating-quantifier statement over $V$, with initial type $b$, block length $\ell(y)$, and input $f(y)$ holds belongs to the alternating class at level $i$ with initial type $b$.
hypotheses_covered: The unary word function determined by $\ell$ is polynomial-time computable
